title: The Great Lakes
objective: After this level you can describe the Great Lakes and how glaciers carved them.
summary: Five lakes, Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie and Ontario, hold about 21% of the world's surface fresh water. Glaciers scoured and deepened their basins, and their water drains east to the Atlantic.

cards.headline: Five lakes hold about 21% of the world's surface fresh water.
cards.body: Split all the fresh water on the world's surface into five equal glasses, and the Great Lakes would fill one of them by themselves. That's a lot of water for one corner of one continent.

cards.headline: Meet HOMES
cards.body: The five Great Lakes are Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie and Ontario. Shuffle their first letters and you get HOMES, the classic way to remember them. Four are shared by the US and Canada; Lake Michigan is the only one entirely inside the US. Together they hold 84% of North America's surface fresh water. Every other lake and river on the continent splits the leftovers.

cards.headline: Dug by ice
cards.body: Where did such giant holes come from? Starting about a million years ago, massive glaciers pushed through the middle of the continent. They scoured existing valleys, widening and deepening them into the basins the lakes now fill. It's Level 7's glacier trick on a giant scale: rivers cut V-shaped valleys, and ice grinds them wider. The glaciers were the diggers. The lakes are what they left behind.

cards.headline: A different door to the sea
cards.body: The lakes aren't a dead end. Their water flows east through the St. Lawrence River into the Atlantic Ocean. Compare that with Level 73's Mississippi, which carries the water south of them all the way to the Gulf of Mexico. Close neighbors on the map, but they leave for the ocean by different doors.

questions.prompt: Which Great Lake lies entirely inside the United States?
questions.explanation: Four Great Lakes are shared with Canada. Lake Michigan is the only one entirely within the US.

questions.prompt: How did the Great Lakes basins form?

options.label: A giant meteorite impact
options.rationale: No impact: ice did the digging.

options.label: Glaciers scoured and deepened old valleys
Volcanoes collapsed into craters
options.rationale: These basins are ice-made, not volcanic.

options.label: The Mississippi carved them
options.rationale: The Mississippi runs south; glaciers dug the lake basins.

questions.explanation: Massive glaciers widened and deepened existing valleys, leaving the basins the lakes now fill.

questions.prompt: From Level 73: the Mississippi reaches the Gulf of Mexico. Where does Great Lakes water reach the sea?

options.label: The Pacific, over the Rockies
options.rationale: The Great Lakes drain east, nowhere near the Pacific.

options.label: The Gulf of Mexico, via the Mississippi
It never leaves the lakes
options.rationale: The lakes drain out through a river.

options.label: The Atlantic, via the St. Lawrence River

questions.explanation: Great Lakes water flows east through the St. Lawrence River to the Atlantic, while the Mississippi heads south to the Gulf.
